transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Helix Head of Alliances), Liam Chen (Helix VP Sales), Maya Patel (Helix Channels Ops)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Um, quick roll call, then we'll jump into the pipeline mapping and the GTM approach.
[00:07] Sofia Ramos: Hi, Sofia here. Excited to get this moving.
[00:10] Liam Chen: Liam — thanks, Jordan.
[00:11] Maya Patel: Maya here.
[00:13] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood, hi all.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Agenda, real quick: 1) share Helix's top joint targets, 2) map co-sell motions — what does success look like, 3) technical blockers (we know VPC and SSO are on the table), 4) next steps and exec intro. Sound right?
[00:28] Sofia Ramos: Yep that's perfect, we also want to align on how logos are credited — that matters for our channel comp.
[00:34] Jordan Lee: Totally, we can put that in the playbook, we'll propose a standard crediting table.
[00:39] Liam Chen: Before we get deep, quick context — Helix is pushing AI automation into three verticals this quarter: medtech, finserv, and logistics. Our partners team flagged Redwood as a good inference partner for the medtech regulated workloads.
[00:53] Priya Nair: Great, just to call out, our Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) is what teams usually pick for PHI/PCI workloads — we have KMS options and audit logs. We'll share the architecture sheet after.
[01:05] Sofia Ramos: Perfect, the medtech deals are the highest priority. We have one active opportunity — "Aster Health" — where the technical security review is upcoming.
[01:15] Jordan Lee: Love it. Can you share the Aster Health brief now? Or put it in the mapping sheet?
[01:19] Maya Patel: I'll add it to the sheet after the call, with stage, ARR estimate, and Helix internal owner.
[01:25] Jordan Lee: Sweet. Ok, let's go account by account. Maya, do you want to walk us through the top six?
[01:30] Maya Patel: Sure. Top 1 is Aster Health — large regional hospital chain, estimated $1.2M ACV if we convert. Top 2 is MeridianPay in finserv, likely $850K. Top 3 is Atlas Freight, logistics, around $420K. Top 4/5/6 are smaller but strategic for logos: Nimbus Research, Cobalt Diagnostics, and Horizon Pharma.
[01:53] Liam Chen: With Aster, timeline is tight — decision committee in early Oct, procurement review first week of Oct.
[02:00] Jordan Lee: That fits a co-sell pilot — we should propose a 6-week POC led by Helix for integration and Redwood for inference. Priya, any technical concerns with a fast POC?
[02:10] Priya Nair: The main items are SSO/SAML integration for their internal users, and network egress restrictions — Aster wants their inference traffic to stay inside a VPC, basically on-prem or VPC-peered. We do VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, but we'll need to confirm latency SLOs with their infra. Also sometimes the transcription of "KV cache" appears in docs as "K V cash" — noticed that in older notes, haha — but it's fine, just a doc quirk.
[02:41] Sofia Ramos: Ha, noted. On the SLOs, Aster's infra team is very sensitive — sub-200ms for clinical workflows is what they want. Is that reachable?
[02:52] Priya Nair: For short sequences and a dedicated GPU pool we can typically get <100-150ms on optimized models, but it depends on tokenization and prompt length. If they need that reliably, we'd recommend dedicated capacity or an on-prem appliance. We should run a quick perf test.
[03:08] Jordan Lee: Ok, perf test as part of the POC. We'll propose a dedicated reserved pool for Aster during the pilot.
[03:15] Liam Chen: On commercial, Helix needs clarity on revenue share for co-sell. Our legal asks for a simple referral credit plus a small reseller margin when Helix does first-line support — what's Redwood's usual approach?
[03:27] Jordan Lee: We usually do a split: either a referral fee for introductions or a revenue share for joint sales where Helix handles integration and first line support. We can put options in the playbook. For enterprise customers we often do a standard co-sell MSA — we'll share a draft.
[03:41] Sofia Ramos: Please share the MSA draft, that helps our procurement.
[03:44] Jordan Lee: Will do.
[03:46] Maya Patel: Quick question on logos: if a customer is procured by Helix but the inference is Redwood hosted, how do we list logos on joint marketing?
[03:55] Jordan Lee: We'll propose mutual logo rights in the playbook with tiers: pilot, customer reference, and case study — each with required approvals.
[04:03] Sofia Ramos: Good.
[04:06] Jordan Lee: Switching gears — competition. Liam, are you seeing Aurora AI or Nebula in the pipeline?
[04:11] Liam Chen: Aurora shows up sometimes in medtech, and CloudRun is a cloud native competitor that claims lower latency at scale. But customers ask about them; we should be ready to position on reliability and SLO-backed offerings.
[04:23] Priya Nair: We have SLA language for Dedicated and Private deployments and an observability console — per-route latency and token cost breakdowns. We'll include screenshots in the deck.
[04:33] Jordan Lee: Great — Priya, can you talk briefly about the handoff model from Helix SE to Redwood SE during a POC?
[04:39] Priya Nair: Yes. Typical: Helix handles ingestion, adapters into the customer's data plane. Redwood provides the inference stack, model selection, and perf tuning. For the POC we embed a Redwood SE as technical owner for 2 weeks and then move to optional weekly check-ins. We also run canary rollouts for model updates to avoid regressions.
[05:00] Sofia Ramos: That sounds like what we need. For Aster they'll want an internal escalation path.
[05:06] Jordan Lee: We'll provide an escalation matrix in the playbook with SE contact and CSM contact.
[05:10] Maya Patel: Does Redwood do cost estimates per token or per session? Helix needs to model margins for channel comp.
[05:18] Priya Nair: We provide token-level cost breakdowns and projected monthly spend for different traffic profiles. We'll add a sample cost model into the spreadsheet so Helix can estimate margins.
[05:27] Liam Chen: Cool. On the technical doc side, Sofia, what do they need for the RfP next week?
[05:33] Sofia Ramos: The procurement team wants architecture diagram, SAML/SSO, data residency, and SOC2 evidence.
[05:40] Priya Nair: We are SOC2 Type II, have audit logs and customer-managed KMS integrations, and can support region restrictions for data residency. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and the SSO how-to.
[05:51] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll drop links in the playbook doc. (link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/partner-playbook/helix)
[05:59] Maya Patel: For the CRM mapping — Helix will export Top 6 and we'll create a joint spreadsheet with stage, estimated ARR, Redwood ask (intro/demo/proof), and Helix owner.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Perfect, that's the center of the co-sell motion. Let's talk pilots: we propose two pilot models — a short "integration pilot" to validate SSO/VPC and latency for Aster, and a second "value pilot" to measure a business metric (e.g., diagnosis triage time improvement). Which should we lead with?
[06:29] Liam Chen: Start with integration pilot, because procurement won't greenlight commercial until they're happy with security.
[06:34] Sofia Ramos: Agreed. For the integration pilot, Helix wants clear deliverables: list of test cases, performance targets, and a go/no-go decision gate.
[06:44] Priya Nair: We'll draft a POC plan template with test cases, including end-to-end latency, SSO auth flows, and model regression checks.
[06:53] Jordan Lee: Timing wise, can Redwood turn that POC template around by Monday 9/20?
[06:57] Priya Nair: Yes.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: Ok.
[07:00] [07:00] Jordan Lee: A quick aside on pricing: for pilots we usually provide trial credits and reduced pilot pricing; for co-sell deals we can discuss channel margin.
[07:10] Maya Patel: On the legal side, procurement will want an NDA and then MSA redlines — can you send a starter NDA?
[07:17] Jordan Lee: Yes, I'll send NDA + MSA starter.
[07:20] Sofia Ramos: Great.
[07:22] Liam Chen: One more question — how do we handle references? We sometimes need a healthcare reference to get procurement comfortable. Does Redwood have a medtech reference that can be used?
[07:32] Priya Nair: We have two healthcare customers who agreed to be references for security and uptime, but we'll need to check with them on availability. Jordan, can you coordinate?
[07:40] Jordan Lee: Yep I'll follow up.
[07:42] Sofia Ramos: Cool, that helps a lot.
[07:46] Jordan Lee: Alright, quick recap of decisions: 1) Helix will export top 6 accounts into CRM mapping sheet; 2) Redwood to send playbook, starter NDA/MSA, SOC2 + SSO docs; 3) Priya to draft POC plan and run perf test proposal for Aster; 4) schedule exec intro for late Sept. Anything missing?
[08:08] Maya Patel: Add: agree to pilot commercial terms — trial credits and reduced pilot pricing.
[08:12] Jordan Lee: Noted.
[08:14] Sofia Ramos: Also, can you include a short training plan for Helix pre-sales engineers? We want enablement before the first pilot kickoff.
[08:22] Priya Nair: We'll include a 2-hour enablement workshop and a tech playbook.
[08:26] Jordan Lee: Great.
[08:28] Liam Chen: Timeline check — Aster procurement first week of Oct, so we need POC signoff and engineering readiness by end of Sept.
[08:38] Jordan Lee: Ok, that's tight but feasible. We'll prioritize Aster in the mapping and POC queue.
[08:44] Sofia Ramos: Sounds good.
[08:46] Jordan Lee: Any final questions?
[08:48] Maya Patel: Not from me.
[08:49] Priya Nair: None.
[08:50] Jordan Lee: Great. I'll send the playbook + docs, Priya will share the tech sheet, and Maya will share the CSV. We'll reconvene after exec intro. Thanks everyone.
[08:59] Sofia Ramos: Thanks all.
[09:00] Liam Chen: Thanks, bye.

Post-meeting notes (auto):
- Document links referenced: https://redwood.ai/partner-playbook/helix (playbook draft), https://redwood.ai/tech/sso-vpc (tech sheets), HubSpot export pending from Helix
- Potential risks: Aster latency requirement <200ms may require dedicated capacity or on-prem variant; procurement timeline is aggressive; need SOC2 evidence and reference availability.
- Suggested next meetings: Exec intro (CRO level), technical deep dive with Aster infra, co-sell pricing review.
